newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Dead, wounded reported in Russian-Chechen clash.
newsitem.headline: Dead, wounded reported in Russian-Chechen clash.

text.p: Russian police and fighters who crossed from separatist Chechnya fought a two-hour gun battle in the southern region of Dagestan, causing casualties on both sides, Interfax news agency said on Tuesday.

The agency quoted Partagen Andriyevskiy, commander of Russian forces in the north Caucasus, as saying some people had been killed in the skirmish near the settlement of Andi just inside Dagestan. It gave no other details of the casualties.
"According to P. Andriyevsky, both sides suffered losses in the battle -- there are dead and wounded," Interfax said.

The report of what would be one of the worst clashes since a ceasefire was agreed in Chechnya last August could not immediately be confirmed independently. Interfax did not make clear when the clash took place.
All crossing points between Dagestan and Chechnya were being closed from 0200 GMT on Tuesday, Andriyevsky said, and border forces were on full alert.
He said the decision had been taken because of "the situation which has become more complicated in the north Caucasus regions bordering Chechnya".
Russian forces say they have detained about 20 "subversive groups" from Chechnya in the past year. Most were detained in the north Caucasus area.
A powerful explosion tore apart a railway station in southern Russia on Monday, killing at least one person and injuring up to 23 in the second suspected bomb blast in five days.
Russian officials said they suspected Chechen separatists were behind the explosion at the station in Pyatigorsk, about 130 km (80 miles) northwest of Chechnya.
Chechen leaders denied the charges and said Russian security forces were responsible, implying that some groups were interested in stirring tensions in the region.
They also denied any involvement in a bomb blast at Armavir railway station in southern Russia last Wednesday which killed two people.
"I categorically declare that the Chechen side did not take part in the terrorist acts on Russian territory," Chechen Vice President Vakha Arsanov told Ekho Moskvy radio station.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin said on Monday he was deeply concerned and made clear relations with Chechnya would deteriorate sharply if a Chechen link was confirmed and the separatist leaders did not crack down in their region.

"The Interior Ministry and Federal Security Service leadership have enough forces and resources to take uncompromising actions and initiatives to stop terrorist acts," presidential spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told Interfax.
The explosion in the first floor waiting room of the station in Pyatigorsk, a spa town in the north Caucasus mountains, blew out windows and badly damaged the roof of the building.
The Emergencies Ministry said one person was killed and 17 were taken to hospital.
Russian news agencies quoted officials in Moscow as saying two people had been killed and up to 23 hurt, but the reports were not confirmed by the ministry.
Chechen leaders, who fought a nearly 21-month conflict with Russian troops over their independence demands, still want full independence. Moscow has ruled out secession.

Radical Chechen guerrilla commander Salman Raduyev has vowed to attack Russia's rail network and other targets to press the campaign for independence. The conflict over Chechen independence has killed tens of thousands of people.
Itar-Tass news agency said Raduyev had claimed responsibility for last week's explosion at Armavir, but more moderate Chechen leaders said they doubted he was behind the attack.
